clue.text: Stop for a time, having finished the development

parts.note: a break is a pause, a stop for a while
to be through is to be done with something

explanation.surface: Someone pauses for a while once a project's development is complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' looks like part of the story about finishing a project, but it is the definition, in its sense of an important new advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden important discovery or advance is a significant development in science or negotiations.

clue.text: Graduate takes a moment to keep particular wine for child

parts.note: Bachelor of Arts, a first degree

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: MO is short for a moment, as in 'half a mo'
a bin is a numbered rack in a wine cellar, so a particular wine is named by its bin

explanation.surface: A graduate pauses briefly to put by a special bottle for a child.
explanation.walkthrough: Wine merchants number their stock by the rack or bin it is kept in, so a bin stands for a particular wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is the Italian word for a baby or small child, borrowed into English informally.

clue.text: Most distant destruction reaches the majority

parts.note: an end is a death or ruin
most means the greater part; 'reaches' is surface padding read as the majority's arrival

explanation.surface: Destruction spreads until it reaches most people, even in the farthest places.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means situated at the very end, farthest away from a point.

clue.text: Gives up pastry as initial impetus

parts.note: to kick a habit is to give it up
a tart is a pastry case with a filling

explanation.surface: Someone on a diet gives up cakes to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-start is a push that gets something moving, named from starting a motorcycle with a foot pedal.

clue.text: Find out time from ticker

parts.note: to hear of something is to learn of it
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone learns the hour by looking at a clock or watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticker' suggests a clock, which fits the time; it is slang for the organ that beats in the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the cardiac organ, from its steady beating.

clue.text: Wind instrument uplifts company using aria without a name

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting up a word reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the song sits around the other letter

parts.note: taken as written; it is split to hold the next piece
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A wind instrument lifts a company's performance of an aria that has no title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a name' reads as lacking a name, but 'without' means outside: OC + ARI(N)A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, often made of clay.

clue.text: Not losing when batting twice in silence

indicators.note: in places the batting inside the word for silence

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them
a batsman at the crease is in, and twice gives two copies

explanation.surface: A cricket team is not losing after batting twice in a quiet ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side currently batting is said to be 'in', so batting twice supplies that word two times.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaining means getting ahead or making progress, the opposite of falling behind.

clue.text: Henry's fourth wife, plainly!

parts.note: a straight description of the fourth queen of Henry VIII
a joke on her reputation: Henry found her unattractive, calling her plain, and the marriage was soon annulled

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plainly' reads as 'obviously', but it also hints at the story that Henry VIII thought this German princess plain when he met her.
explanation.definitionFit: The German princess married Henry VIII in 1540 as his fourth queen; the union was annulled within months.

clue.text: Retired friend of Pythias in charge of travelling

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Damon and Pythias are the legendary Greek pair of loyal friends
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A retired classical figure, Pythias's friend, is in charge of journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon and Pythias are the Greek byword for loyal friendship; Damon offered his life as surety for his friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic describes people who wander from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: NT liar nearly declared grandmother to be backward

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the combined letters from right to left
nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: said means stated or declared
nana is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: A New Testament liar barely admitted that his grandmother was a slow learner.
explanation.walkthrough: SAID loses its D to give SAI; SAI + NANA is then reversed. NT is the New Testament, where Ananias lies to Peter in Acts 5.
explanation.definitionFit: In Acts, Ananias lied to the apostles about the price of land he sold and fell dead.

clue.text: Char passed round lake without help

indicators.note: round says the first word surrounds the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: to char is to scorch or singe
L is the abbreviation for lake
to hand something is to pass it

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady handed a cloth around a lake on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' suggests a charwoman (a cleaner) or tea, but it is the verb meaning to scorch: SING(L)E + HANDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something single-handed means achieving it alone, with nobody assisting.

clue.text: Newspapermen could be so tired

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may turn into something else

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Journalists might well be exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors are the senior journalists who run a paper and decide what goes in it.

clue.text: Education will switch it in and out

indicators.note: to switch things around is to change their order

parts.note: the words it, in and out taken as written; 'and' only joins them

explanation.surface: Schooling will flick a switch on and off.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, especially given to a pupil or small group.

clue.text: Petty cash needed but none in a bedsitter

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the word for a rented room

parts.note: a bedsitter is a small one-room flat
none is nothing, a zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A tenant needs spare cash but has none in their little rented room.
explanation.walkthrough: FL(O)AT. A bedsitter, or bedsit, is a British one-room rented home.
explanation.definitionFit: A float is a small sum of money kept for change or minor expenses, like a till float.

clue.text: Russian port calls for chief backer

parts.note: arch means principal, as in arch-enemy
an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatre show

explanation.surface: A Russian harbour needs a main financial supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel, or Arkhangelsk, is a seaport on the White Sea in northern Russia.

clue.text: Carbon once put outside this place for sticking together

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: put outside says one word wraps around another

parts.note: taken as written; it is split to hold the next piece
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Carbon was once placed outdoors here to see whether it would stick together.
explanation.walkthrough: C + O(HERE)NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherence is the quality of holding together, physically or logically, as cohesion.

clue.text: Desperate for telephone system, one held by fastening

indicators.note: held by means gripped inside something else

parts.note: a latch is a fastening on a door or gate
STD is subscriber trunk dialling, the old British direct-dial phone system
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is desperate to get a phone line, one with a lock on it.
explanation.walkthrough: LA(STD I)TCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch attempt is a final desperate effort made when everything else has failed.

clue.text: Bess needs IOU to get change for onion sauce

indicators.note: change says the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bess needs a written promise of debt so that she can buy a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' sounds like coins handed back; here it rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Soubise is a French sauce of puréed onions in béchamel, named after the Prince de Soubise.

clue.text: Beautiful rhyme like "Your Obedient Servant"!

parts.note: surface: a lovely piece of verse; setter's reading: a word that rhymes with the adjective beautiful
the old formal sign-off for a letter, promising obedience and respect

explanation.walkthrough: There is no letter-by-letter wordplay: the answer rhymes with 'beautiful' and describes the obedient servant of the old formal letter ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means obedient and respectful, doing what one ought, as a loyal servant does.

clue.text: Farm operated by church

parts.note: to run a business is to operate it
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A farm is run by the local church.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one in North America raising cattle.

clue.text: Broken reed about to pose when moved

indicators.note: broken means split open, so the word is parted to let something in
about means surrounding the following word

parts.note: taken as written
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A snapped reed is about to be posed for a picture after being shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' suggests an anagram, but the reed keeps its letters in order and is only split into two halves to hold the pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Resited means placed in a new location, relocated to another site.

clue.text: Lion's tail is wrapped in fat with a deafening roar

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the end of the word lion

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed by the following word

parts.note: oily means greasy or fatty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lion's tail is caught in grease and it roars.
explanation.walkthrough: N + O(IS)ILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisily means making a great deal of sound, as a loud roar does.

clue.text: Athlete in cellar, turning again

parts.note: a vault is an underground cellar

indicators.note: turning round means reading the short word in the opposite direction

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: An athlete is down in a basement, spinning round once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link here: the definition sits beside the wordplay, not inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaulter is an athlete who jumps with a pole or over a horse in gymnastics.

clue.text: What's kindled again in obscure literature?

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A question about what fires up again in hard-to-read books.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindled again means set on fire for a second time, which is what relighting a fire does.

clue.text: "Urn" is as translated into this language

indicators.note: translated means turned into a different form

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The word 'urn' is rendered as a word in a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' suits a language clue, so it hides its anagram job well.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian is the Slavonic language of Russia, spoken by well over a hundred million people.

clue.text: Much alcohol puts king in wrong

indicators.note: puts ... in means placing one thing inside another

parts.note: sinful means morally wrong
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Heavy drinking puts a monarch in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: S(K)INFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinful is informal British slang for enough drink to make someone drunk.

clue.text: American tree goes headlong

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: An American tree falls over head first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headlong' looks like one word but splits into head and long.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut pines are North American pines, such as the piñon, whose seeds are eaten.

clue.text: Churchman turns dry ready-mix in church festival?

indicators.note: turns means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an elder is an official in some Protestant churches

indicators.note: to mix things is to jumble them up

parts.note: TT is teetotal, abstaining from drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church official spins a dry readymade mixture during a religious feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready-mix' looks like one product, but 'mix' is the anagram signal for ready. The question mark is there because a red-letter day was originally a saint's day marked in red in the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Church calendars printed feast days in red ink, hence a special or memorable day.
